study.title: Remedy, the work
study.stance: The handoff is part of the design. A product this regulated ships only as well as it is handed over.

chapters.title: A pharmacy agent for Shoppers Drug Mart
body: Remedy is the PC Health AI agent: refills and renewals, appointment booking, answers with sources, and a pharmacist when a person should take over.

Design, prototyping and agent strategy ran from January to August 2026. Version one launched on iOS in June. The national launch added booking for several patients, vaccines, weight management, web and Android.

chapters.title: One request, two outcomes, one conversation
body: Pharmacy runs on rules: refill or renewal, patient or caregiver, which store, which medication. The golden path was set as the hardest common case. A caregiver asks for refills. One medication is eligible, another needs a renewal. The agent resolves both before the chat ends, and offers to follow up.
Every flow starts from a person's own words, never from a menu.

image.alt: Rx refill screens: a caregiver's request resolved as one refill and one renewal in the same conversation

chapters.title: Safety as a surface, not a disclaimer
body: Answers show where they came from. Long answers stay readable. When a conversation needs real care, red-flag escalation hands it to a person, plainly and quickly.
Trust is built in the response itself, not in a banner above it.

image.alt: Citations on a Remedy answer, showing the sources behind it

chapters.title: One agent, contextual credentials
body: Separate assistants for health and shopping were becoming two relationships with one customer. The direction became a single agent with one name and one context. The voice stays the same. The authority changes with the moment: a pharmacist's sign-off in health, the store in commerce.
The rule that came with it: a consent beat before any suggestion to buy, and a conversation that ends on care, not the sale.

image.alt: The Remedy chat core: composer, response and thinking states

chapters.title: Thirteen questions for what comes next
body: Beyond the launch, thirteen studies, each a question with a method and a signal to watch. How the agent says its first hello. Whether it can build a family profile without a form. What a tasteful handoff from a health question to a shopping one looks like. What makes switching from ChatGPT feel like an upgrade instead of starting over.
Each is measured by what people do, not what they say they liked.

image.alt: Still from the first hello test, an agent introducing itself

chapters.title: The handoff, as a product
body: Fourteen features, four libraries, thirteen Labs studies and the source files, each card one click from its design on every platform. A spreadsheet is the source of truth, so the site changes without code. Built so engineering, and whoever picks this up next, can find anything in seconds.
This is that site, as it was delivered.

study.title: A trusted helpdesk for Botpress
study.stance: Support agents will do more than answer. They will fix the broken link, refund the late box and ship the change, once someone trusts them to. Lily is how that trust gets built, one approval at a time.

chapters.title: Agents will take on more and more of the helpdesk
chapters.change: Sooner or later, every helpdesk will be able to do this. A team will only hand the work to the one it trusts.

steps.label: Where support is going
steps.title: Support people move up a layer
steps.why: Support is full of tasks AI can already help with, and the list keeps growing. One by one the work moves to agents, and the people who did it move up: directing the agents and stepping in where a person matters most.

steps.label: Building trust
steps.title: Nobody hands over a whole support operation on day one
steps.why: No one asks an agent to run everything from the start. Each task it handles reliably earns it the next, slightly bigger one. It proves itself on the small stuff before anyone hands it the big stuff.

steps.label: Onboarding
steps.title: First impressions establish trust
steps.why: The first steps up the line happen in onboarding: helping set up, introducing Desk, suggesting what to do next. That is where trust starts, from day one.

steps.label: Lily
steps.title: Build that trust in Lily
steps.why: Lily already helps people inside Botpress. If those early steps happen with Lily, the relationship lives in her. Every small win adds to it, so she is the one people trust as the stakes rise, all the way up to running Desk.

study.title: Remembering, with permission
study.stance: An agent should be useful enough to feel like it knows you, and restrained enough that it never feels like it's watching.

chapters.title: Memory, designed as a list instead of a promise
body: PC Chat remembers health facts drawn from conversation: a condition, a medication, an allergy, a pregnancy. What shipped handles the moment someone tidies their data, with lists, menus and confirmations. It barely touches the points where trust is decided: when a memory is made, how long it lasts, and how it is let go.
The brief that followed was wider than one product: design the relationship, the points of contact and the feelings in them, not just the screens.

chapters.title: Every rule sits between two failures
body: Trust, between forgetful and presumptuous. Emotion, between cold and creepy. Interaction, between interruptive and buried. Transparency, between black box and overexplained. Twelve ideas, three per tension, each with a principle, a test, and a real moment from PC Chat scored against it.

chapters.title: Remember with permission
body: The gap: someone mentions a vaccine to get booster advice, and PC Chat saves it as a memory. A pill appears afterwards. There is no moment to agree. The fix proposes the memory under the answer and waits for Save.

image.alt: Remember with permission: a 'Remember this for next time?' prompt beside the PC Chat screen that saved a memory without asking

chapters.title: Saying no is free
body: Declining should never cost more than accepting. Removing one memory meant a red dialog, with a box that also deleted the whole chat. The fix: Won't remember this, with an undo. Dialogs stay for bulk, irreversible deletes.

image.alt: Saying no is free: a quiet 'Won't remember this · Undo' toast beside the delete dialog it replaces

chapters.title: Forget gracefully
body: Chats auto-delete after 60 days. Memories, including "8 weeks pregnant", never expire. Facts go stale, and some become painful. Time-bound memories get an expiry and a quiet "Still true?" check-in.

image.alt: Forget gracefully: a 'Still true?' check-in on a pregnancy memory ten months later

chapters.title: Leave the chat
body: Chat is one surface. Refills and booking were designed only as conversations, with no notification, widget or Live Activity. Pickup status belongs on the lock screen; chat is for questions.

image.alt: Leave the chat: a pickup notification on the lock screen, where routine needs belong

chapters.title: Show the working
body: Where PC Chat gets it right: "1 memory used" sits beside "2 sources" under an answer and opens the exact memory that shaped it. Personal context, cited like any other source.

image.alt: Show the working: an answer citing two sources and one memory used

chapters.title: 13 gaps, 10 supports, 3 mixed
body: The gaps cluster in two places: when a memory is made, and how long it lasts. Transparency is strongest. Each idea carries an empty lane for the next product, so the framework outlives this one.
